subject: RunLevelData vs ProcessedData objects after normalization: different results

messages.author: b01272b519db217a
messages.subject: RunLevelData vs ProcessedData objects after normalization: different results
parts:
Dear MSstats dev team,

I am reporting an observation that I just had regarding what seems to be slightly different results between RunLevelData and ProcessedData objects after dataProcess, and ask for your recommendation on which would be the better output to use if one wants to export the summarized+normalized protein abundances from MSstats into an expression matrix in order to continue running the statistics on a different pipeline (i.e. for clustering analysis or multi-variate linear modeling).

Visualization of log2intensities by Protein/Experimental group from the RunLevelData object

normalized_data <- dataProcess(msts_formated_data)

tab_proccessed_data <- normalized_data$RunlevelData

hist(tab_proccessed_data$LogIntensities, 
     main = "Normalized Intensities by Protein from 'RunLevelData'")



ggplot(data = tab_proccessed_data,
       aes(x = GROUP_ORIGINAL, y = LogIntensities)) +
   geom_boxplot() + 
   ggtitle("Normalized Intensities by Condition from 'RunLevelData'")


It can be noticed an extreme outlier is present

dataProcessPlots(normalized_data, 
                 type = "QCplot", 
                 which.Protein="allonly",
                 address = FALSE)


The outlier is not noticed when using the function dataProcessPlots

Visualization of log2intensities by Protein/Experimental group from the ProcessedData object

The ProcessedData object was further processed to get the mean Log2 Intensities values per Protein per Run.

tab_proccessed_datatest <- normalized_data$ProcessedData

to_wide <- tab_proccessed_datatest %>% 
   select(PROTEIN, ABUNDANCE, GROUP_ORIGINAL, SUBJECT_ORIGINAL) %>%
   mutate(GROUP_REPLICATE_RUN = paste0(GROUP_ORIGINAL,"_",SUBJECT_ORIGINAL)) %>%
   group_by(PROTEIN, GROUP_REPLICATE_RUN) %>% 
   summarise(LogIntensities = mean(ABUNDANCE)) %>%
   ungroup() %>% 
   separate(col = GROUP_REPLICATE_RUN,
            sep = "\\_",
            into = c("Group", "Replicate_run"))

hist(to_wide$LogIntensities, 
     main = "Normalized Intensities by Protein from 'ProcessedData'")



ggplot(data = to_wide,
       aes(x = Group, y = LogIntensities)) +
   geom_boxplot() + 
   ggtitle("Normalized Intensities by Condition from 'ProcessedData'")


The outlier is not observed when using the ProcessedData object and further processing to get the mean Log2Intensities of features per Protein per Run.

Is there an explanation for this to happen?

Noticing this, what would make more sense to use if one wants to export a summarized and normalized expression matrix after processing with MSstats? I have been using the RunLevelData object for this purpose but now it seems that there is an outlier filtering step happening before the ProcessedData object is created.

In the same context of this question: is there an argument against using the mean of the log2 intensities of the features per protein per run to get the normalized intensities per protein per run for downstream analysis?

Many thanks as always for taking a look into this and for the MSstats development.

Best wishes,
Miguel

messages.author: b01272b519db217a
messages.subject: Re: RunLevelData vs ProcessedData objects after normalization: different results
parts:
Hello,

On the same order of ideas as before. I just quickly checked for similarities between the summarized protein values and missingness between the two objects. The mean log2 intensties are the same, bet there are considerably more missing values coming from the ProcessedData object.



Best wishes,
Miguel

messages.author: bc13a282f8b0c08b
messages.subject: Re: RunLevelData vs ProcessedData objects after normalization: different results
parts:
Hi,



currently, the ProcessedData slot of dataProcess() output does not include intensities updated in the imputation step. This is fixed in the development version (github.com/Vitek-Lab/MSstats-dev, develop branch) and will be fixed in the next Bioconductor release. After that update, ProcessedData matches the input to RunlevelData.



Kind regards,
Mateusz
